name: Rara Mutton
blurb: Punjabi mutton curry cooked with mutton mince for a thick, double-meat gravy.

steps.text: Brown the onions slowly in ghee with the whole spices.
Add ginger-garlic paste and the mutton; sear well. Add the powders, tomatoes and yogurt.
Cook covered until the mutton is nearly tender.
Add the mince and cook until done and the gravy is thick. Finish with garam masala, kasuri methi and coriander.

name: Chicken Saagwala
blurb: Chicken cooked in spiced spinach purée.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach with the chillies and blend it.
Crackle the cumin; brown the onions, add ginger-garlic paste, then the chicken.
Add the tomato and powders; cook until the chicken is nearly done.
Add the spinach and simmer five minutes; finish with garam masala, kasuri methi and cream.

name: Methi Chicken
blurb: Chicken curry with fresh fenugreek leaves and a little kasuri methi.

steps.text: Crackle the cumin; brown the onions, add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the chicken, powders and tomatoes; cook on high.
Stir in the yogurt and methi leaves; cover and cook until done.
Finish with kasuri methi and garam masala.

name: Tinda Masala
blurb: Round gourd cooked soft in onion and tomato. A Punjabi summer vegetable.

steps.text: Crackle the cumin; soften the onion and ginger.
Add the tomatoes and powders; cook down.
Add the tinda and half a cup of water; cover and cook until soft.
Finish with amchur, garam masala and coriander.

name: Paneer Do Pyaza
blurb: Paneer with onions two ways: cooked into the gravy and tossed in at the end.

steps.text: Sear one onion and the capsicum in big pieces; set aside.
Crackle the cumin, brown the other onions and add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and powders; cook to a thick masala.
Add the paneer, the seared onion and capsicum, kasuri methi and garam masala.

name: Kathal Ki Sabzi
blurb: Young jackfruit cooked like meat in a spiced onion masala.

steps.text: Boil the jackfruit pieces with turmeric and salt until just soft; fry them golden.
Fry the whole spices and onions until brown; add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes, powders and yogurt; cook down.
Add the jackfruit and a little water; simmer and finish with garam masala.

name: Bharwa Karela
blurb: Bitter gourds stuffed with onion and a tangy spice mix, cooked slowly until crisp.

steps.text: Scrape the gourds, slit them and rub with salt; rest 20 minutes, then rinse and squeeze.
Fry the kalonji and onions until golden; add all the powders.
Stuff the gourds with the mix and tie with thread.
Cook them in mustard oil on low, covered, turning until soft and crisp outside.

name: Arbi Fry
blurb: Boiled taro roots flattened and fried crisp with ajwain and amchur.

steps.text: Boil the arbi until tender, peel and press each one flat.
Toss with the powders and salt.
Fry in oil with the ajwain until crisp on both sides.
Sprinkle with chaat masala.

name: Soya Chunk Curry
blurb: Soya chunks in an onion and tomato gravy. Cheap, filling and high in protein.

steps.text: Boil the soya chunks for five minutes, rinse in cold water and squeeze dry.
Crackle the cumin; brown the onions and add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and powders; cook down.
Add the chunks and a cup of water; simmer and finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: Lobia Curry
blurb: Black-eyed peas in an onion, tomato and garlic gravy.

steps.text: Soak the lobia for six hours and pressure cook until soft.
Crackle the cumin and hing; brown the onion, add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and powders; cook down.
Add the lobia with its water; simmer and finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: Kala Chana Curry
blurb: Black chickpeas in a thick spiced gravy.

steps.text: Soak the chana overnight and pressure cook until soft.
Crackle the cumin and bay leaf; brown the onions, add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and chana masala; cook down.
Add the chana and some cooking water; mash a few and simmer. Finish with amchur and coriander.

name: Veg Kolhapuri
blurb: Mixed vegetables in Kolhapur's hot coconut and sesame masala.

steps.text: Roast the coconut, sesame, chillies, whole spices and one onion; grind with water.
Boil or steam the vegetables until just done.
Fry the other onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes with turmeric and Kolhapuri masala.
Add the paste, vegetables and water; simmer and finish with coriander.

name: Yakhni Pulao
blurb: Rice cooked in the stock of mutton and whole spices. Plainer than biryani, with more flavour in the grain.

steps.text: Tie the coriander, fennel and pepper in muslin. Boil the mutton with it, half the whole spices, one onion and ginger-garlic paste until tender.
Soak the rice for 30 minutes.
Fry the rest of the whole spices and the other onion in ghee; add the mutton and yogurt and cook two minutes.
Add the rice and 3 cups of the stock; cook covered on low until done. Top with fried onions.

name: Matar Pulao
blurb: Basmati and green peas cooked with whole spices. Goes with any dal or curry.

steps.text: Soak the rice for 30 minutes.
Fry the cumin, whole spices and bay leaf in ghee; add the sliced onion until golden.
Add the peas and rice; stir gently for a minute.
Add three cups of water and salt; cover and cook on low until done.

name: Tawa Pulao
blurb: Mumbai's street rice tossed on the big tawa with pav bhaji masala and vegetables.

steps.text: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate; cool it.
Fry the cumin and garlic in butter; add the onion, capsicum, peas and tomatoes and cook soft.
Add the pav bhaji masala, chilli powder, turmeric and salt.
Toss in the rice; finish with lemon and coriander.

name: Rava Fish Fry
blurb: Fish steaks rubbed with spice and coated in semolina, fried crisp.

steps.text: Rub the fish with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, lemon and salt. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the sooji and rice flour.
Press each piece into the coating on both sides.
Shallow fry until crisp and cooked through.

name: Murgh Musallam
blurb: A whole chicken stuffed with boiled eggs, marinated and slow-cooked in an onion and nut masala.

steps.text: Prick the chicken all over and rub it with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala and salt. Rest two hours.
Grind the cashews, almonds, poppy seeds and fried onions to a paste. Boil and peel the eggs and stuff them inside the chicken.
Brown the chicken in ghee on all sides. Add the whole spices, the paste and the marinade.
Cover and cook on low, turning now and then, until tender. Add saffron milk at the end.

name: Bhuna Gosht
blurb: Mutton slowly fried with onions and spices until almost dry and dark.

steps.text: Brown the onions slowly with the whole spices.
Add ginger-garlic paste and the mutton; fry on high until coloured.
Add the powders, tomatoes and yogurt; cook covered on low, adding a splash of water when it sticks, until tender.
Uncover and keep frying until the masala is dark and clings. Finish with garam masala, pepper and coriander.

name: Sindhi Kadhi
blurb: Sindhi vegetable curry thickened with roasted besan and soured with tamarind. No yogurt.

ingredients.label: Drumsticks, okra, potato, cluster beans and carrot

steps.text: Fry the cumin, fenugreek, mustard and curry leaves; add the besan and roast on low until brown.
Slowly whisk in five cups of water; add the tomatoes, ginger, chillies, turmeric and chilli powder.
Add the vegetables and simmer until tender.
Add tamarind water and salt; simmer five minutes. Finish with coriander.

name: Sai Bhaji
blurb: Sindhi spinach cooked with chana dal and vegetables, mashed together. Eaten with rice.

steps.text: Soak the chana dal for an hour.
Fry the cumin, onion, ginger and garlic; add the dal, vegetables, greens, tomatoes and powders.
Add a cup of water and pressure cook until everything is soft.
Mash with a whisk until coarse.
